modern: Speak both in the senate and to every man, whoever he may be, appropriately, without any affectation: use plain speech.
original: Speak both in the senate and to every man, whoever he may be, appropriately, not with any affectation: use plain discourse.

notification_original: Speak both in the senate and to every man, whoever he may be, appropriately, not with any affectation: use plain discourse.

explained.summary: Speak plainly and appropriately to everyone, whether in the Senate or to an ordinary person. Skip the affectation and the airs. Marcus wants the same honest, straightforward way of talking whatever the audience.
explained.today: It means not putting on the jargon in a presentation, not talking down to the person at the till, and not changing your voice to impress the important guest at dinner.
